title: add downgrade-guard + pre-upgrade checks + backup/restore improvements for private installer
author: Sasha Kim
release_notes: Adds a downgrade guard to the private installer, improves pre-upgrade checks and backup/restore flow, introduces schema migration safety gates, and pins component versions for deterministic upgrades.
description: Motivation: Recent upgrade incidents showed we lacked deterministic version pinning and pre-upgrade safety checks for Private deployments which caused partially applied schema migrations and difficult rollbacks. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to make upgrades safer: 1) version pinning for critical components in Helm and Terraform so operator-controlled upgrades are deterministic; 2) a downgrade guard that prevents installing older operator versions when newer schema versions are present; 3) a pre-upgrade check command (installer cli: preflight upgrade-check) that validates backups, migration status, and active connections; 4) safer Postgres schema migrations that write a migration ledger and support a two-phase apply with an automatic abort path if health checks fail; 5) backup/restore improvements that include an offline snapshot mode and verification steps to ensure restore integrity; 6) a documented rollback path and automated rollback helpers which attempt to re-apply a compatible previous release and restore from a verified snapshot when needed. This change touches the Helm charts (templates and values defaults), Terraform modules (version variables and provider pinning), installer CLI (new subcommands and flags), migration tooling (migration-ledger table and guard checks), and the upgrade docs. Compatibility: all new behaviors are behind a feature gate (ENABLE_UPGRADE_SAFETY=true) and default to enabled for new installs. Testing: added end-to-end upgrade tests using the perf-canary harness in a mini-cluster and integration tests for the CLI preflight flow. Rolling forward: the implementation is designed to be backward-compatible if the feature gate is turned off, but operators are encouraged to enable it for improved safety. See commits and review thread for details and rationale.

review_comments: Priya Desai: Could we make the downgrade guard opt-in for existing clusters by default? I want to avoid unexpectedly blocking operator re-installs.

Sasha Kim: Good call. Implemented as a feature gate ENABLE_UPGRADE_SAFETY which we default to true for new installs but leave off for existing clusters unless explicitly enabled. Added a migrate-check that warns but doesn't block if gate is off.
Evan Liu: The migration ledger is great, but we should ensure the ledger writes are idempotent and survive partial failures. Add retry and idempotency checks.
Sasha Kim: Added idempotent upsert semantics and a retry loop with backoff for ledger writes. Also added a health check that will abort the two-phase apply if any ledger entries are inconsistent.
Marco Alvarez: Terraform changes need a clear upgrade note—operators using pinned module versions may need to re-run terraform init with the new constraints. Add release notes.
Sasha Kim: Documented the terraform init step and added an automated check in the preflight step that warns if provider versions differ from the pinned constraints.
changelog_entry: Added upgrade safety features for Private installer: version pinning, downgrade guard, preflight upgrade checks, safer DB migrations with migration ledger, offline backup/restore verification, and an upgrade runbook (admins should read docs/private-upgrades.md).
notes_for_ops: - ENABLE_UPGRADE_SAFETY defaults to true for fresh installs; set to false to opt-out on existing clusters. - Run 'installer preflight upgrade-check' before attempting upgrades. - Always take an offline snapshot using 'installer backup --offline' for stateful clusters. - Terraform users: run 'terraform init -upgrade' if providers are already pinned to older versions. - Restoration uses verified snapshots; restore will abort if verification fails.
